IN THE PROCESS THE HOSE WAS LEFT UNATTENDED AND FELL OUT OF THE DRUM SPILLING OIL INTO THE SPILL CRATE, SOME OF WHICH REACHED ATLANTIC OCEAN. ALTHOUGH THE INCIDENT OCCURRED 1505 EST THE VESSEL WAS UNABLE TO REPORT UNTIL 1804 EST DUE TO COMMUNICATION ISSUES WHILE UNDERWAY.

properties.content:
Report Details
NRC Report ID: 1045551
Incident Time: 2013-04-30 08:55:00
Nearest City: Baltimore, MD
Location: MAIN GATE, USCG YARD 2401 HAWKINS POINT RD.
Incident Type: STORAGE TANK
Material: GASOLINE: AUTOMOTIVE (UNLEADED)
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: U.S. COAST GUARD YARD
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 39.333333, -76.950000 (Explicit)
Reported Spill Volume: 3 gallons
Report Description
***WEB REPORT*** A GOVERNMENT VEHICLE (PICK-UP TRUCK) FROM CGC SLEDGE WAS ENTERING THE COAST GUARD YARD WITH A 5 GL GASOLINE CONTAINER IN THE BED OF THE TRUCK. THE CONTAINER WAS NOT SECURED AND THE GASOLINE SPILLED IN THE BED OF THE TRUCK AND LEAKED ONTO THE ROADWAY AT THE MAIN GATE. THERE WAS A SHEEN APPROX. 40' X 4' LEADING TO A STORM DRAIN, WHERE APPROX. 8 OZ. OF GASOLINE ENTERED THE DRAIN. THE CG FIREHOUSE CREW RESPONDED WITHIN 5 MINUTES OF THE SPILL AND PLACED ABSORBENT MATERIAL AROUND THE STORM DRAIN AND ALL THE WAY BACK TO THE ORIGIN. THE ABSORBENT MATERIAL WAS LEFT APPROX. 10 MIN. TO ABSORB THE GASOLINE, THEN WAS SWEPT UP & PLACED IN PLASTIC BAGS FOR PROPER DISPOSAL THROUGH THE YARD'S DLA CONTRACTOR.

SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 47.271061, -122.373826 (Approximated from premise)
Reported Spill Volume: 48000 gallon
Report DescriptionTHIS IS A POTENTIAL RELEASE... UPDATE TO NRC REPORT 1298295 BASED ON INFORMATION FROM NATIONAL COMMAND CENTER AND SECTOR PUGET SOUND: THE F/V ALEUTIAN FALCON CONTINUES TO BURN AT THE PIER (PIER 25, NOT 24 AS PREVIOUSLY STATED) WITH FIREFIGHTERS FIGHTING FROM THE SHORE AND FROM THE WATER, BUT ARE UNABLE TO BOARD. IT WAS LEARNED THAT ALEUTIAN FALCON HAS APPROXIMATELY 90 TO 100 POUNDS OF AMMONIA ON BOARD. DUE TO THIS, STATION SEATTLE IS ENFORCING A 1500-YARD SAFETY ZONE AROUND THE VESSEL. A VESSEL IN THE IMMEDIATE VICINITY WAS TOWED TO SAFETY. ALEUTIAN FALCON WAS REPORTED TO HAVE CRACKS IN THE HULL AND A 15 TO 25 DEGREE LIST. THERE WAS ALSO REPORTED TO BE 48,000 GALLONS OF DIESEL ON BOARD THE VESSEL. AN OIL SPILL RESPONSE ORGANIZATION, THE MARINE SPILL RESPONSE CORPORATION, HAS BEEN CONTRACTED AND IS RESPONDING. SECTOR PUGET SOUND POLLUTION RESPONDERS ARE ON SCENE. A BOOM HAS BEEN PLACED AROUND THE VESSEL. A COAST GUARD OVERFLIGHT WILL LIKELY TAKE PLACE IN THE MORNING. A FOLLOW-ON CIC WILL BE HELD AT 1300 Z. ORIGINAL REPORT IS BELOW: THIS IS A POTENTIAL RELEASE... CALLER REPORTED A VESSEL FIRE AT THE HYLEBOS MARINA. CALLER STATED THE CAUSE OF THE FIRE IS UNKNOWN. THERE IS A POTENTIAL RELEASE OF AN UNKNOWN OIL TO THE HYLEBOS WATERWAY.
